dump: I've been thinking for weeks about whether to rewrite our backend in Go or keep shipping features on the Python monolith. The monolith is slow and painful but at least I know it. Go would be faster but it's a 3-month rewrite and we have no Go experience. I'm scared of choosing wrong.
Should I quit my job and go freelance? I have two clients lined up but no safety net. My current job is stable but soul-crushing. I keep going back and forth every weekend.
My co-founder and I disagree about pricing. She wants to charge enterprise prices from day one. I think we should start free and prove value. We've been avoiding the conversation for a month.
I need to decide whether to raise a seed round now or wait until we hit $10k MRR. Investors are interested but we'd dilute early. If we wait, we might run out of runway in 4 months.
My team keeps asking me to pick a project management tool — Notion, Linear, or Jira. Every time I try to decide I get overwhelmed by the options and just postpone it. It's been two months.
Do I hire a senior engineer now (expensive, might not survive our next round) or keep relying on contractors (flexible but slow and disconnected)? My instinct says hire but my spreadsheet says wait.
I've been offered a role at a big tech company — great salary, interesting work, but I'd have to shut down my startup which has real users. I don't know if I'm tired or if I'm just afraid.
My co-founder wants to pivot to B2B. I built this for consumers and it still feels right. But we have zero consumer revenue after 8 months. I don't know if I'm being principled or deluded.
I can't decide whether to move the team to fully remote or require two days in office. Half the team hates commuting. The other half says async kills culture. I keep delaying the announcement.

We have a partnership offer from a larger company. It would give us distribution but they'd have exclusivity for 18 months. I'm worried about locking us in. But without it we might not survive the year.
